llm.summary: This is a disclosed PatentMax cloud client that generates paid patent-competition reports, with some privacy and local-cache considerations but no evidence of malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: Bash, Read, and Write fit the workflow, but users should understand that optional materials files may be read and uploaded to api.ip930.com for report generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, package install, remote code retrieval, or dependency bootstrap was found; the script uses Python standard library only.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are mostly bounded to parameter confirmation, paid-task consent, polling, and conservative reporting; Chinese-only user-facing messages are a usability/locale limitation, not a security violation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script stores a trial key and task records under ~/.patentmax and writes reports/results to the output directory; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no cron, startup service, or backdoor behavior found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: it submits company, technology direction, objectives, and optional materials to PatentMax, then downloads a Word/JSON report.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending patent-analysis inputs, company names, objectives, markets, and any optional background files to api.ip930.com. Do not upload confidential diligence materials without approval, verify cost before allowing --yes, and expect a local ~/.patentmax cache for the trial key and task state.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The API key is used as a Bearer token for the declared PatentMax API; I found no broad environment dump or unrelated credential transmission.
[LP1] expected: Outbound HTTPS to api.ip930.com is central to the cloud-report workflow and is repeatedly documented, though a clearer permission/privacy notice would help.
[E1] expected: External transmission of report inputs and optional uploaded materials is real and sensitive, but it matches the stated service purpose and is not hidden.
[RA2] expected: The persistence evidence is limited to local trial-key and task-state files used to resume/download reports; no autonomous agent, scheduled task, or startup persistence was present.
[SQP-3] expected: The skill is predominantly Chinese and relays service messages in Chinese; this is a locale limitation users should know, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[SDI-4] expected: The documentation mixes descriptive competitive analysis with high-level decision support, but it also warns against guaranteed conclusions, legal conclusions, and layout-strategy advice.
